root_causes: Inefficient repeated high-level action selection (e.g., repeated Rearrange[sushi_mat_0, on, table_29] and Rearrange[ramekin_1, on, table_29]) despite the action already being in progress or effectively achieved.
Poor coordination between agents leading to unnecessary Wait[None] actions instead of parallelizing object transfers more effectively.
Delayed recognition of successful subgoal completion (progress only credited at S803 and S915) causing extra navigation and rearrange attempts before updating the completed propositions.
Overly conservative replanning behavior (multiple replan_pre/post_window cycles) that added planning overhead without meaningfully changing the plan.
improvement_suggestions: Add a stronger termination condition for high-level rearrange actions so that once an object is on or effectively being placed on the target table, the planner stops issuing the same Rearrange command.
Improve subgoal state monitoring so that completion of each object transfer (sushi mat, ramekin, spoon) is detected and credited as soon as the object is correctly placed, avoiding redundant steps.
Enhance multi-agent coordination to reduce idle Wait[None] usage by allowing both agents to carry and place different objects concurrently whenever possible.

Tune replanning triggers to avoid unnecessary replan_pre_window / replan_post_window cycles when the current plan is already progressing, thereby reducing planning overhead and negative reward accumulation.
overall_assessment: The task was ultimately completed successfully with all objects moved to the entryway table, but the trajectory contained redundant rearrange and wait actions, leading to inefficiency and a relatively high negative total reward.
task_instruction: Move the sushi mat, ramekin, and spoon from the dining room table to the entryway table.
